clues: This city stands on a thumb of land that juts into a broad harbor. The sea wraps it on most sides, past bays and inlets.
Cold sea storms, called nor'easters, can bury this coast town in snow. Winters are cold and stormy, with spells of heavy snow and rain.
Puritan settlers crossed to this shore in 1630 and founded the town. A pact one year before had set up their bay colony, led by its first governor.
In 1773, angry townsfolk threw a whole shipment of tea into the harbor. They fought a tax they hated, and the act fired up a revolution.
The laws of Massachusetts are made in this city. It is the state capital, and the state's largest city too.
